objective: Al terminar enfatizas lo que dices con do/does/did, so/such, 'on earth', 'at all', 'the very', pronombres reflexivos y adverbios intensificadores.

warmup.prompt_es: El énfasis da fuerza y emoción a tus frases. Aprendes los recursos del inglés para insistir, corregir, expresar sorpresa o transmitir intensidad, tanto hablando como escribiendo.

text: A night I will never forget

I do remember the exact moment the storm started. We were sailing off the coast of Portugal when the sky suddenly turned black. The waves were so high that the boat began to rock violently. It was absolutely terrifying.
'What on earth are we going to do?' I shouted. My brother, who never panics, did look worried this time. 'Nothing at all,' he replied. 'We just have to hold on.'

I had never been so frightened in my life. It wasn't the wind itself that scared me; it was the darkness. Never before had I felt so small. But we did survive, and the very next morning the sea was perfectly calm, as if nothing had happened.

I myself still can't believe it. What I learned was how quickly nature can change. I'm not saying I'd never sail again; I'm saying I'd think twice before doing it without a proper weather forecast. And I did make one promise: never again without a life jacket!
input.es: Una noche que nunca olvidaré. Recuerdo perfectamente el momento exacto en que empezó la tormenta. Navegábamos frente a la costa de Portugal cuando el cielo se puso de repente negro. Las olas eran tan altas que el barco empezó a balancearse violentamente. Fue absolutamente aterrador. '¿Qué demonios vamos a hacer?', grité. Mi hermano, que nunca entra en pánico, esta vez sí parecía preocupado. 'Nada en absoluto', respondió. 'Solo tenemos que aguantar.' Nunca en mi vida había tenido tanto miedo. No fue el viento lo que me asustó, sino la oscuridad. Jamás me había sentido tan pequeño. Pero sobrevivimos, y a la mañana siguiente el mar estaba perfectamente en calma, como si no hubiera pasado nada. Yo mismo todavía no puedo creerlo. Lo que aprendí es lo rápido que puede cambiar la naturaleza. No digo que no volvería a navegar; digo que lo pensaría dos veces antes de hacerlo sin un pronóstico del tiempo adecuado. Y sí hice una promesa: ¡nunca más sin chaleco salvavidas!

md_es: **Recursos para enfatizar**
| Recurso | Cómo se usa | Ejemplo |
| **do / does / did + base** | afirmar con fuerza o contrastar | *I do like it. · She did call you.* |
| **so + adj / such (a) + sust.** | intensidad | *It was so cold! · It was such a cold night.* |
| **adverbios intensificadores** | refuerzan adjetivos | *absolutely, completely, utterly, extremely, incredibly* |
| **on earth / the hell / in the world** | sorpresa o enfado en preguntas | *What on earth are you doing?* |
| **at all / whatsoever** | refuerzo negativo | *I don't like it at all. · There is no evidence whatsoever.* |
| **the very + sustantivo** | justo ese | *The very idea scares me. · The very next day.* |
| **pronombre reflexivo** | énfasis en la persona | *I myself saw it. · The manager himself called.* |
| **inversión tras adverbio negativo** | énfasis formal | *Never before had I felt so small.* |
| **cleft (it is… that)** | enfatizar un elemento | *It was the darkness that scared me.* |
**Adverbios intensificadores**
- Con adjetivos *absolutos* (no graduables): *absolutely terrifying, completely impossible, utterly exhausted, totally wrong.*
- Con adjetivos *graduables*: *very cold, extremely tired, incredibly cold.*
- ✘ *absolutely cold* → ✔ *absolutely freezing*; ✘ *very terrifying* → ✔ *absolutely terrifying.*
**So y such**
- *so + adjetivo/adverbio: so cold, so quickly.* · *such + (a/an) + (adjetivo) + sustantivo: such a cold night, such waves.*
- *so many / so much + sustantivo: so many people, so much noise.*
- Consecuencia: *so… that / such… that: It was so cold that we stayed in.*
**Inversión con adverbios negativos (formal)**
- *Never before had I felt so small. · Rarely do we see such waves. · Not only did we survive, but we also learned something.*
**Errores típicos**
- ✘ *It was very terrifying.* → ✔ *It was absolutely terrifying.*
- ✘ *She did called me.* → ✔ *She did call me.*
- ✘ *It was so a cold night.* → ✔ *It was such a cold night.* / *It was so cold a night.*
- ✘ *I don't like it none at all.* → ✔ *I don't like it at all.*
- ✘ *Never I had seen it.* → ✔ *Never had I seen it.*
**Ojo:** *do + verbo* no se usa con *be* (*I'm tired* → *I am tired*, no *I do am*). En la escritura, el énfasis con cursiva o negrita; en el habla, con entonación: *I DID call you!*
Pronunciación: *absolutely* /ˈæbsəluːtli/ · *violently* /ˈvaɪələntli/ · *whatsoever* /ˌwɒtsəʊˈevə/ · *earth* /ɜːθ/.
